items.title: Sakana AI's self-improving model gets better at solving and judging, but can't catch its own blind spots
items.description: Sakana AI's MASS method lets one language model improve itself by solving tasks, judging results, and refining workflows, reaching a win rate of nearly 70 percent against the base model after two rounds. But when the model misses the same errors across all three roles, it can mistake them for progress and reinforce them during training. items.title: Meta releases its first frontier model, Muse Wonder
items.description: Where Muse Spark aimed to be a lightweight model that could perform at low latency, the Wonder models are larger and said to be more capable, with higher benchmark scores and better results on complex tasks like coding.

items.title: Clearing chat history helps AI agents find better solutions
items.description: Microsoft researchers found that autonomous AI agents get trapped in what they call "idea basins" because of their growing chat context, local solution regions they can't escape. Their "Fork-and-Flush" method clears the chat history but keeps the workspace, achieving up to 66 percent better results on the same compute budget. The article Clearing chat history helps AI agents find better solutions appeared first on The Decoder .

items.description: Andrej Karpathy, co-founder of OpenAI and now at Anthropic, sees a widening knowledge gap in AI.
